clauses.current_legal_basis: Continuing under the original_plus_bounded_search route: the held original as amended by the two held later instruments (Executive Order 9242-A and Executive Order 14085 section 1); the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (release point 119-121, edition current through 2026-10-09) prints the order as amended by both and states no ending; the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog name no revocation or supersession, and the order has no own-terms end.

later_events.mechanism: amendment (restatement of the first paragraph): before, the first paragraph described service in any capacity in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard; after, it describes service in any capacity in or with those forces; the rest of the paragraph (establishment of the Air Medal with ribbons, date of September 8, 1939, meritorious achievement while participating in an aerial flight) is repeated unchanged

amendment (strike and insert, with a new final paragraph): first paragraph, before: Army and Navy, any person, distinguishes or has distinguished himself, forces listed without the Air Force and Space Force; after: Armed Forces, those individuals, distinguish or have distinguished themselves, Air Force and Space Force added; second paragraph, before: design approved by the Secretaries of War, the Navy and the Treasury and award by those Secretaries, and Coast Guard awards under the Navy's jurisdiction; after: design approved by the Secretary of Defense, award by the Secretaries of the Army, the Navy, the Air Force or the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, and Coast Guard awards under the jurisdiction of the Navy; new final paragraph: regulations of the Secretaries of the military departments on the award shall be uniform so far as practicable and subject to the approval of the Secretary of Defense. Reviewer note: the substance of the second paragraph's award authority changed, while the establishment of the medal and the one-medal rule continue

clauses.reason: The sole clause is the order as a whole: the establishment of the Air Medal, the design-approval and award authority, and the one-medal rule with bars or devices and posthumous presentation. It was not terminated by any held instrument. Executive Order 9242-A restated the first paragraph and Executive Order 14085 further amended the first and second paragraphs and added a final paragraph; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, and both amendments are recorded as later events with the text before and after. The held U.S. Code note prints the order as amended on a release point current through 2026-10-09 with no ending statement, no held source revokes or supersedes the order, and the order has no duration or condition of its own, so the clause was operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register original (7 FR 3541, PDF page 1; text file EO_9158 of the fr-originals job) is Executive Order 9158, Air Medal, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt on May 11, 1942 (F. R. Doc. 42-4314, filed May 12, 1942); the number, title and date agree with the register row. The order has one inventory clause covering its three paragraphs. Two held later instruments amend the order and neither ends it. Executive Order 9242-A (signed September 11, 1942; 7 FR 7874) restated the first paragraph so that service in or with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard qualifies. Executive Order 14085 section 1 (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541) further amended the first and second paragraphs by striking and inserting words (Armed Forces, Air Force and Space Force, those individuals, approval of the design by the Secretary of Defense, award by the Secretaries of the Army, the Navy and the Air Force or the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, and Coast Guard personnel serving under the jurisdiction of the Navy) and added a final paragraph on uniform regulations. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, and each amendment is a later event that records the text before and after. Current law: the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (Office of the Law Revision Counsel release point 119-121, edition current through 2026-10-09) prints the order as amended by both instruments and states no ending; the order has no duration, condition or sunset of its own. Route original_plus_bounded_search: the held original, both held later instruments, no own-terms end, and the three bounded searches after reading their coverage notes. The U.S. Code search found one hit, the note above; its edition ends 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected, which is disclosed here and is not a ground to doubt a presidential order that no held source ends. The eCFR search (point in time as of 2026-10-14) found no hit. The Federal Register catalog notes held for this order are an Amended-by note naming EO 9242-A, a See note naming Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948 (13 FR 8163), and the Amends note under EO 14085; none is a revocation or supersession. The order was unrevoked and operative on 2026-10-14.

savings.reason: No clause ended and nothing was revoked, so there is no ended command whose awards or effects need saving; the order as amended remains the instrument establishing the Air Medal, and the held U.S. Code note prints it as amended by Executive Order 9242-A and Executive Order 14085 without any ending statement.
